strategies.overview: Terrakion is a superb wallbreaker and hyper offense lead, using its excellent Speed tier, immediate power, great offensive typing, and utility moves like Stealth Rock, Swords Dance, and Taunt to great effect. Focus Sash lead Terrakion can often disrupt opposing leads, like Jirachi and Krookodile, with Taunt before establishing its own entry hazard and potentially racking up damage with its powerful STAB attacks. Swords Dance Terrakion is incredibly threatening, as it can comfortably break past walls like Chesnaught and Hippowdon once they've taken a bit of chip damage. Terrakion does compete with other Fighting-types though, struggling to fulfill the role with stiff competition like Mienshao and Galarian Zapdos, which both have U-turn and Knock Off. While other hyper offense leads offer more utility, such as Healing Wish Jirachi and Endeavor Lycanroc, Terrakion remains a great option as a lead, setup sweeper, and wallbreaker.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Sacred Sword is an alternative to Close Combat that can surprise IronPress foes like Registeel. X-Scissor can be used to slice through bulky Psychic-types like Reuniclus and Slowbro, which is especially beneficial on Swords Dance sets.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types: Reuniclus and Slowbro can notably stomach Terrakion's attacks and threaten it back with Psychic Noise and Scald, both of which can comfortably 2HKO it. Armarouge, if positioned well against a Close Combat, can use Weak Armor to potentially reverse sweep. Cresselia and Necrozma can also sponge attacks from Terrakion well and threaten to set up or take it out.

Faster Wallbreakers and Revenge Killers: While Terrakion is generally fast, it is easily outpaced by other wallbreakers like Barraskewda and Choice Scarf users like Gardevoir and Galarian Zapdos; the latter two can find safe entry points against it, as they resist Close Combat.

Physical Walls: Hippowdon can be an annoyance for Terrakion, comfortably sponging its attacks and threatening to KO it back with Earthquake or phaze it with Whirlwind. Chesnaught can sponge any attack from Terrakion and threaten to KO it back with Body Press.

Golurk: While pretty niche, Golurk counters most Terrakion sets, threatening to KO it with ease, while Terrakion can't do much back.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Thanks to its high Attack stat and almost unresisted STAB combination, Choice Band Terrakion makes for an excellent wallbreaker that is very difficult to switch into. Earthquake helps it deal with Jirachi and is a great option for picking up weakened targets without suffering from the defense drops or inaccuracy from its STAB moves. Quick Attack gives it a form of priority to deal with faster, weakened Pokemon like Cyclizar and Noivern. Justified allows Terrakion to switch into Dark-type attacks and punish moves like Knock Off from Cyclizar to boost its Attack. Tera Blast paired with Tera Ghost gives Terrakion a Ghost-type move that threatens a 2HKO on bulky Psychic-types like Slowbro and Reuniclus. Tera Rock boosts Terrakion's Stone Edge even further, making it very difficult to switch into and guaranteeing a 2HKO on Slowbro. Tera Rock helps Terrakion defensively by removing its weaknesses to Fairy and Psychic and giving it a resistance to Flying-type attacks, making it much better into revenge killers like Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Talonflame. Tera Ghost also removes its weaknesses to Fairy and Psychic, but it also removes its weaknesses to Fighting and Ground, which gives Terrakion an opportunity to take out common Choice Scarf users such as Mienshao, Galarian Zapdos, and Krookodile. Tera Ghost pairs well with Justified, deterring opposing Pokemon from hitting it with super effective Dark-type attacks in fear of boosting its Attack.

Choice Band Terrakion can fit on a plethora of balance and bulky offense teams thanks to its great Speed tier and its excellent power as a wallbreaker. Entry hazard support from Pokemon like Chesnaught, Empoleon, and Krookodile can help it pick up 2HKOs on bulky physical walls like Hippowdon and Slowbro and rack up residual damage on revenge killers like Choice Scarf Gengar and Krookodile switching in. Terrakion appreciates pivot support to get it in safely; therefore, Pokemon like Cyclizar and Jirachi can keep up momentum by pivoting on defensive switch-ins like Empoleon and Krookodile and create opportunities for Terrakion to attack. Terrakion appreciates Future Sight support from Pokemon like Slowbro and Reuniclus, as it can use Close Combat more freely while Future Sight punishes Fairy-, Flying- and particularly Poison-types that switch in like Amoonguss, Noivern, and Gardevoir. Lots of common Choice Scarf users such as Gardevoir, Galarian Zapdos, and Mienshao can revenge kill Terrakion, making defensive partners that can switch into the aforementioned Pokemon very valuable. Physical tanks such as Hippowdon and Slowbro and special walls like Empoleon can switch into the revenge killers while offering utility like entry hazards and Rocky Helmet chip damage. Terrakion weakening opposing Pokemon like Hippowdon, Jirachi, and Hisuian Goodra allows teammates like Choice Scarf Krookodile and Gyarados to come in afterwards and finish the job.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description:
Swords Dance Terrakion is a powerful setup sweeper, which boasts almost immediate wallbreaking power. Earthquake acts as an excellent coverage move and allows it to deal with targets such as Jirachi and Golurk easily. Substitute is an alternative that lets Terrakion safely choose whether to set up a Swords Dance or fire off a STAB move after forcing out a Pokemon like Cyclizar or Bisharp. Taunt can be used to stop entry hazards from going up and take away recovery and other status moves from foes such as Hippowdon and Slowbro. Air Balloon earns Terrakion a free turn against Ground-types such as Krookodile and can be used alongside Taunt to completely shut down Hippowdon without Stone Edge. Leftovers is an alternative that allows Terrakion to take better advantage of its decent natural bulk and synergizes particularly well with Substitute. Tera Flying removes its weaknesses to Ground- and Fighting-type attacks, thus giving it opportunities to set up against as well as break checks like Hippowdon, Chesnaught, and Choice Scarf Krookodile.

Swords Dance Terrakion fits best on offense structures, particularly hyper offense, due to its ability to threaten the majority of the metagame after a single Swords Dance. It shares many of its defensive checks, like Hippowdon, with other common setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Mimikyu. This means that Terrakion can often be sacrificed to deal good damage to these checks before fainting, which enables the aforementioned sweepers to capitalize on the weakened physical walls to potentially pull off a sweep. Its great Speed tier strengthens its ability to chunk holes in the opposing team by taking advantage of common Pokemon like Jirachi and Krookodile, which can often free up teammates like Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Weak Armor Armarouge to clean up late-game. It pairs well with specially offensive wallbreakers and setup sweepers such as Nasty Plot Gengar and Calm Mind Armarouge, which can KO common Terrakion checks like Slowbro, Hippowdon, and Chesnaught with ease. Terrakion offers valuable support to teammates like Gengar and Maushold that fear Knock Off greatly, as its ability, Justified, acts as a strong deterrent against it. In addition, Terrakion can work well as a cleaner in entry hazard-stacking team structures, which try to wear down opposing teams, alongside setters such as Jirachi, Gligar, and Chesnaught, as many defensive Pokemon, such as Amoonguss and Suicune, only need to be chipped marginally to be in Terrakion's KO range after a Swords Dance.

movesets.name: Stealth Rock
movesets.description:
Set Details

Terrakion is an effective lead for hyper offense teams due to its good Speed and great offensive presence, especially against common entry hazard removers like Cyclizar and Maushold. Rock Blast is generally used over Stone Edge to circumvent opposing Focus Sash leads, including Kleavor, though Terrakion is still unfortunately slower than Froslass and Ribombee. Swords Dance makes Terrakion a major wallbreaking threat, hindering physical walls like Hippowdown, Chesnaught, and Gastrodon that look to dampen Terrakion's impact as an offensive lead. Taunt inhibits opposing hazard leads like Jirachi, setup users such as Slowbro and Suicune, and Defog Noivern. Focus Sash best ensures Terrakion a turn to set up Stealth Rock or attack. Loaded Dice synergizes with Rock Blast, guaranteeing Terrakion can OHKO Kleavor and giving it a better chance to OHKO Mimikyu through its Disguise. Tera Ghost lets Terrakion spinblock, and the additional Fighting immunity can surprise Mienshao and opposing Terrakion.

Stealth Rock set up by Terrakion enables other hyper offense staples, including Armarouge and Maushold. Defiant users, such as Bisharp and Galarian Zapdos, are especially noteworthy for punishing Defog users. Armarouge and Gardevoir can also take advantage of Talonflame for Terrakion. Moxie Gyarados particularly appreciates entry hazards chipping down foes so it can more easily start to snowball. Mimikyu is another common pick for hyper offense teams, and its Ghost typing helps preserve Terrakion's hazards against Cyclizar while deterring Maushold. Other Ghost-types, such as Gengar and Hisuian Zoroark, can similarly spinblock, and they pressure Psychic-types like Slowbro, Reuniclus, and Mew for Terrakion.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Terrakion's high Speed and access to perfect coverage mean that it is an ideal Choice Scarf user that outspeeds most other Choice Scarf users in the tier, making it an excellent revenge killer. Earthquake helps it deal with Jirachi and is a great option for picking up weakened targets without suffering from the defense drops or inaccuracy from its STAB moves. Rock Slide gives Terrakion a more reliable Rock-type move to use by trading power for accuracy. Stealth Rock allows Terrakion to act as an entry hazard setter that is able to get it up on Pokemon it forces out like Choice Scarf Krookodile locked into Knock Off. Justified allows Terrakion to switch into Dark-type attacks and punish moves like Knock Off from Cyclizar to boost its Attack. Tera Rock helps Terrakion by boosting its Rock-type moves, helping it clean up versus foes that don't resist Rock and threatening a 2HKO on Amoonguss after Stealth Rock. Tera Ground boosts Earthquake's damage and threatens an 2HKO on Golurk while granting it an immunity to common Thunder Wave support like Reuniclus and Cresselia.

Choice Scarf Terrakion fits best on balance and bulky offense teams, as it is a great revenge killer that can outspeed common Choice Scarf users like Gardevoir and Krookodile. Chesnaught and Hippowdon make for good partners that offer utility like entry hazards and Rocky Helmet chip damage that weaken the opposing Pokemon and make it easier for Terrakion to clean. Sand Stream Hippowdon can also set up sandstorm for Terrakion, giving it a Special Defense boost and allowing it to switch into special attacks it normally shouldn't. Terrakion struggles into strong physical walls like Hippowdon, Slowbro, and Chesnaught, which can stop it from cleaning, so bulky partners like Noivern, Talonflame, and Wo-Chien are appreciated, as they can take hits for Terrakion and force these walls out. Wallbreakers like Crawdaunt and special attackers like Magnezone and Hisuian Zoroark can also weaken the aforementioned walls while making it much easier for Terrakion to clean up. Future Sight support from Slowbro and Reuniclus makes it harder for physical walls to switch in and particularly punishes Poison-types such as Amoonguss, allowing Terrakion to use its STAB moves more often instead of locking into Earthquake.

movesets.name: Choice Band (Rock)
movesets.description:
Choice Band Terrakion is one of Rock's best physical wallbreakers thanks to its high Attack, good Speed, and Fighting-type STAB moves, which allow Rock teams to threaten opposing Steel-types like Archaludon and Heatran. Close Combat threatens opposing Dark- and Steel-types such as Ting-Lu, Bisharp, and Corviknight. Earthquake complements Terrakion's Rock-type STAB attacks and targets bulky threats like Toxapex, Clodsire, and non-Air Balloon Gholdengo. Upper Hand allows Terrakion to handle priority moves that it is weak to from Pokemon like Scizor and Breloom while dealing considerable damage to them. Sacred Sword is also an option as a secondary Fighting-type STAB move that doesn't have the drawback of dropping Terrakion's defenses and can ignore Defense boosts from Pokemon like Archaludon. Rock Slide also can be used as a secondary Rock-type STAB option due to its higher accuracy than Stone Edge and chance of flinching.

Hisuian Arcanine is a good teammate for Terrakion, as both Pokemon work well offensively in dismantling Steel-type teams' defensive cores. Terrakion's Close Combat can OHKO Heatran and Archaludon, and Arcanine's Flare Blitz OHKOes Gholdengo and does significant damage to Corviknight and Skarmory. Tyranitar offers a Special Defense boost to Terrakion via its ability Sand Stream, allowing it to tank special attacks it is weak to like Enamorus and non-Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast, letting Terrakion OHKO them in return. In conjunction with entry hazard support in Stealth Rock, Tyranitar's sand is able to chip down opposing walls like Pecharunt, which is 2HKOed by Earthquake after Stealth Rock and sand damage. Terrakion also appreciates Tyranitar's Psychic immunity, which allows it to check threats to Terrakion such as Mew, Indeedee, and Deoxys-S. Ogerpon-C is an essential teammate, threatening opposing Water- and Ground-types like Toxapex, Hippowdon, and Great Tusk thanks to its Grass typing. Glimmora offers Spikes support, which enables Terrakion to break defensive walls like the aforementioned Hippowdon and Great Tusk more easily. Its Poison typing also assists in getting rid of Toxic Spikes, improving Terrakion's longevity, and its Mortal Spin helps Terrakion stay healthy throughout the game, allowing it to switch in without the worry of taking damage from Spikes. Terrakion appreciates Iron Boulder's Speed tier, which threatens Pokemon like Meowscarada, Ogerpon-H, and Choice Scarf Enamorus that Terrakion is slower than and OHKOed by. Iron Boulder also threatens opposing Fighting-types like Sneasler and Keldeo thanks to its Psychic typing. Choice Scarf Kleavor is able to set up Stealth Rock without fear of Magic Bounce using Stone Axe, which helps helps Terrakion deal more damage, and it is able to outspeed threats to Terrakion like Flutter Mane. Kleavor's U-turn can also bring in Terrakion safely. Minior offers a Ground immunity thanks to its Flying typing, and it appreciates Terrakion's ability to break through its checks like Toxapex so it can set up and sweep late-game with Shell Smash.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (Rock)
movesets.description:
Swords Dance Terrakion is an immensely strong wallbreaker for Rock teams thanks to its incredible STAB combination in conjunction with its good Speed that lets it outspeed common threats to Rock teams such as Iron Treads, Garchomp, and Landorus. Stone Edge allows Terrakion to nail Primarina and Gliscor that could otherwise take on Close Combat. Close Combat complements Stone Edge perfectly and is Terrakion strongest STAB attack, allowing it to target Steel-types such as Archaludon and Iron Treads. Upper Hand lets Terrakion circumvent priority such as Breloom's Mach Punch, Scizor's Bullet Punch, and Keldeo's Vacuum Wave, with +2 Upper Hand OHKOing Scizor and Keldeo after Stealth Rock damage and always OHKOing Breloom. Alternatively, Earthquake can be used over Upper Hand, allowing Terrakion to more easily threaten Gholdengo, Toxapex, and Clodsire super effectively. Life Orb allows Terrakion to clock important OHKOs, such as on Corviknight and Galarian Weezing with Close Combat and Stone Edge, respectively, after Stealth Rock chip damage and a Swords Dance boost.

Hisuian Arcanine forms a potent wallbreaking core with Terrakion against Steel teams. Hisuian Arcanine can also threaten physically defensive Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Sinistcha for Terrakion; In return, Terrakion can weaken some of its checks like Archaludon, Swampert, and Gliscor. Ogerpon-C can threaten Ground- and Water-type Pokemon for Terrakion, such as Hippowdon, Great Tusk, and Primarina, as well as being able to beat common shared checks with Terrakion, such as Toxapex and Landorus-T. Iron Boulder can deal with Poison- and Fighting-types for Terrakion; such as Pecharunt, Okidogi, and Keldeo. Iron Boulder can also use a Choice Scarf to revenge kill faster Pokemon that would otherwise outspeed Terrakion such as Iron Valiant, Meowscarada, and Sneasler. Tyranitar can set hazards up as well as check Psychic-type Pokemon such as Latios and Latias for Terrakion. In return, Terrakion can deal with common Steel-types such as Archaludon and Iron Treads for it. Glimmora can scare out Fairy- and Grass-types such as Hatterene, Clefable, and Hydrapple while also providing Toxic Spikes, which can chip down targets such as Iron Hands and Garchomp, as well as hazard remova, which helps Terrakion not get worn down by hazards. Garganacl can switch into most walls such as Corviknight, Amoonguss, and Toxapex and force progress against them with Salt Cure. Purifying Salt lets it absorb status effects that may be aimed at Terrakion, such as Toxic from Clodsire and Will-O-Wisp from Sableye and Dragapult. Shell Smash users such as Drednaw and Minior appreciate Terrakion's ability to punch holes into the opposing team so that they can sweep more effectively.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description: Choice Band Terrakion is a fearsome wallbreaker thanks to its good Attack stat, useful offensive typing, high-Base Power STAB moves, and ability to bypass Fluffy. Earthquake allows Terrakion to hit non-Earth Eater Gholdengo and have a slightly stronger and more accurate option against foes like Iron Hands and Pecharunt. Terrakion's last moveslot is very flexible, as it likes to use Close Combat or Stone Edge almost all of the time. Stealth Rock can help wear down the opposing team and chip would-be defensive checks into range of a 2HKO, while Quick Attack can pick off faster, weakened foes, and Poison Jab does more damage to Primarina and Scream Tail. Teammates such as Iron Boulder, Zamazenta, and Roaring Moon appreciate Terrakion's ability to break through Corviknight, which is one of their biggest roadblocks, and can clean up weakened teams. Terrakion is vulnerable to being revenge killed due to its middling Speed stat, so a strong defensive backbone featuring Pokemon like Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Manaphy is recommended. Terrakion fits best on balance and bulky offense teams that need a wallbreaker and can help it switch in safely, so slow pivots like the aforementioned Corviknight and Manaphy make for good teammates. Additionally, special pivots like Azelf and Hisuian Electrode can get it in on special walls such as RegenVest Meloetta and Hisuian Goodra, which it can threaten out.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 5 onwards

Price Range: 9-10 points

Overview: Terrakion is a solid middle-of-the-road wall breaker and revenge killer. The fact that its STAB moves give it almost near-perfect coverage allows it to function great in both of these roles while also freeing up moveslots for more niche sets. Unfortunately, Terrakion's offensive typing is very weakness-laden defensively. This means that its teammates need to pick up the slack on the defensive side. The only defensive benefit Terrakion really brings is to function as a Knock Off absorber, as resisting Dark and getting an Attack boost after getting hit can be beneficial for its teammates.

Common Roles

Wallbreaker: Terrakion's combination of its STAB moves and high Attack stat coupled with its above-average Speed stat means it can act as a solid wallbreaker. With Rock / Fighting providing near-perfect coverage, this frees up its other moveslots for coverage, utility, or Swords Dance.

Revenge Killer: Terrakion's solid Speed stat coupled with a Choice Scarf can turn it into a very potent revenge killer. Access to a great combination of STAB moves allows it to revenge kill a solid portion of the metagame.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Stone Edge, Close Combat, Sacred Sword, Rock Blast, Rock Slide

Setup Moves: Swords Dance

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Smack Down, Brick Break, Substitute, Taunt, Roar

Coverage: Earthquake, Zen Headbutt, X-Scissor, Poison Jab, Iron Head, Quick Attack, High Horsepower

Niche Moves

Endure: Endure is often paired with Salac Berry, allowing Terrakion to effectively boost its Speed on wallbreaking and setup sets.

Reversal: Reversal is combined with Endure and commonly Salac Berry to turn Terrakion into a potent late-game cleaner.

Upper Hand: Upper Hand has a usable niche on Swords Dance sets when Terrakion is faced with strong priority users, allowing it to turn the tide against them and beat them one-on-one.

Common Items

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf is commonly used to turn Terrakion into a great revenge killer, allowing it to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame. Furthermore, this doubles as a late-game cleaner, exploiting holes made in the opposing team.

Choice Band: Choice Band is used to push Terrakion's already respectable wallbreaking capabilities to another level. This allows it to punch holes in the opposing team as well as clean up once holes have been punched.

Niche Items

Damage-boosting Items: Damage-boosting items can help Terrakion elevate its power without the drawbacks of a Choice item, allowing it to punch holes into the opposing team without losing its flexibility in moves. Damage-boosting items are also used on Swords Dance sets to allow for specific OHKOs after a boost.

Lum Berry: Lum Berry is mostly used on Swords Dance sets where foes can threaten to cripple it with burn or paralysis, allowing Terrakion to ignore them once.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots is always a solid item in matchups where Terrakion does not need to boost its damage output or act as a revenge killer. It is also an option on Swords Dance sets, as they allow Terrakion to set up more than once if the need for that arises.

Salac Berry: Salac Berry is Terrakion's only option to boost its Speed without being locked in a move. It can reliably be activated via Substitute or Endure.

Resistance Berries: Terrakion can benefit from Resistance Berries to take a hit and set up or trade with a faster foe.

Focus Sash: Focus Sash can be used on Terrakion to turn it into a suicide lead that sets up Stealth Rock, punch a hole into an opposing foe via its hard-hitting STAB attacks, or reliably set up a Swords Dance.

Tera

Terrakion is a decent Tera Captain; however, it is only really used as a secondary Tera Captain, as its cost allows it to be paired with better Tera Captains. If you make Terrakion a Tera Captain, it can benefit from defensive Tera Types to shore up its terrible defensive profile. Tera Steel, Water, and Ghost can all grant it a free turn to fire off its high-powered attacks, whereas Tera Fighting boosts its Fighting-type STAB attacks to a whole new level.

Draft Strategy

Terrakion is an offensive Pokemon through and through. Its defensive profile means that its teammates should pick up the slack, so it appreciates a solid defensive backbone. Terrakion's ability to punch holes into an opposing team means that late-game cleaners excel with it, and additional offense can allow it to be a fantastic cleaner in its own right.

Slow Pivots: Terrakion's middling bulk means it loves having a slow pivot to get it in safely, as that allows it to fulfill its role to the best potential. Corviknight, Galarian Slowking, and Moltres can all perform this role greatly while also supporting other teammates.

Dark- and Ghost-types: Dark-types help Terrakion get rid of Ghost-types that can freely switch into its Fighting-type STAB moves. Ghost-types fulfill the same role with the granted benefit that they tend to get hit by Dark-type moves, allowing Terrakion to get a boost from Justified. Meowscarada, Gholdengo, and Weavile are all excellent partners for Terrakion.

Late-game Cleaners: Terrakion's ability to punch holes into the opposing defenses means that late-game cleaners can have an especially good time at closing out games. Iron Valiant, Gouging Fire, and Raging Bolt all can fulfill this role greatly. They can also switch roles where they punch holes and Terrakion functions as the late-game cleaner.

Entry Hazard Setters: While Terrakion can run Stealth Rock, it prefers another teammate for this role, as that frees up space in what it can do. Every form of entry hazard helps Terrakion, and the chip they deal can turn a 2HKO into a OHKO. Teammates such as Galarian Slowking, Glimmora, and Great Tusk all can help with this.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-Types: Terrakion relies on Choice items, allowing Ghost-types to come in for free and get a free turn when Terrakion uses its Fighting-type moves. This means that Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Sinistcha that can set up can use this free turn to become a scary threat.

Faster Pokemon: While Terrakion's typing provides it with a great offensive profile, its defensive profile leaves something to be desired. This means that a lot of common types hit Terrakion for super effective damage with a bunch of scary attackers being faster than it. Meowscarada, Iron Valiant, and Serperior all threaten to cleanly OHKO it.

Strong Priority Users: Terrakion has a weakness against some of the strongest priority users in the format, which means that they can come in and revenge kill most versions of Terrakion. Bullet Punch from Scizor, Jet Punch from Palafin, Aqua Jet from Hisuian Samurott, and Mach Punch from Breloom are some common STAB priority attacks that Terrakion is weak against.

Status: Terrakion needs both its Speed and Attack to function in every role it commonly wants to fill, meaning it is especially susceptible to both burn and paralysis. These statuses are especially scary when coming in on the switch. Hisuian Zoroark, Rotom-W, and Galarian Weezing-are some premiere status spreaders that have a good matchup into Terrakion.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Rock)
movesets.description: Terrakion is the ideal Choice Scarf user for Rock teams due to its high Speed stat and access to powerful coverage moves in Earthquake and Close Combat. Close Combat provides coverage against Steel-, Normal-, and Dark-types such as Heatran, Mega Lopunny, and Greninja. Earthquake does heavy damage against Electric-types such as Zeraora and Tapu Koko as well as against Poison-types like Toxapex and Clodsire. Poison Jab is able to pressure Grass- and Fairy-types that Rock teams struggle to deal with, being able to OHKO Tapu Bulu and Whimsicott as well as deal high amounts of damage to Azumarill and Tapu Lele. Choice Scarf allows Terrakion to be an amazing revenge killer, outspeeding threats like Mega Lopunny and Zeraora. Terrakion pairs well with Shuckle, as its Stealth Rock and Sticky Web support allows Terrakion to net more KOs and outspeed faster Pokemon like Regieleki, Choice Scarf Meowscarada, and Adamant Barraskewda under rain. Terrakion also pairs well with Mega Diancie, which softens the likes of Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Toxapex for Terrakion thanks to its coverage. Alolan Golem helps Terrakion with the Steel matchup by trapping Pokemon such as Mega Scizor, Corviknight, and Celesteela with its ability Magnet Pull. Nihilego is able to help with the Fairy matchup with Sludge Wave dealing big damage to Pokemon such as Tapu Fini and Clefable. Tyranitar helps Terrakion by setting up sand, which boosts Terrakion's Special Defense stat, allowing it to survive Surf from Choice Scarf Greninja and Dazzling Gleam from Tapu Koko. Tyranitar also provides Pursuit support against faster Choice Scarf users such as Latias while also being able to break walls for Terrakion, allowing it to clean teams more easily.
